messages:
IncidentBot: PAGER: Dedicated GPU pool eu-west-1-resv-3 has hit 100% reserved utilization. Queue growth observed for reserved-capacity jobs. Autoscaler failing to provision new nodes: rate-limited API errors. Affected tenants: KestrelHealth (enterprise, reserved), several dev sandboxes. Please acknowledge and join #incident-bridge if available.
Sam (oncall): acked. i'm on it — pulling metrics and launching bridge. linking ops-bridge: https://meet.link/ops-4547774321 :phone: 
Anya (sre): seeing sustained enqueue rate ~420 reqs/min for reserved queue; queue length at 2.3k, median latency > 6s for start-of-inference. autoscaler logs show 429 from cloud quota endpoint: 
``` 
2026-03-15T21:12:05Z autoscaler ERROR scale_up failed: quota_exceeded (429)
2026-03-15T21:12:11Z autoscaler WARN retrying backoff=30s
``` 
Mike (platform): tagging -- i just checked capacity planner, we hit per-account GPU region limit for our infra account in eu-west-1. We have cold GPUs available in eu-west-2 but cross-region provisioning is slow (~8-12m). 
Jordan (cs): KestrelHealth is on a reserved contract and reports failing inference jobs. They DM'd support: "latency spikes and queue 5xx". Need to avoid SLA breach. What temporary mitigations can we do fast? 
Eli (runtime): recommending immediate fallback to smaller quantized model for Kestrel's traffic (can drop quality a bit but reduces GPU memory and concurrent slot usage). Also can enable per-tenant throttles to protect reserved pool for prioritized tenants. 
Sam (oncall): doing two things in parallel: (1) open a quota increase request to cloud provider (ticket created: CLOUD-REQ-9872) and (2) apply emergency routing to send non-critical reserved sessions to hosted fallback models in region eu-west-1-hosted. 
Anya (sre): note: hosted fallback will increase per-token cost but preserves latency. To enable, we need a routing rule change in control plane: add policy route for tenant:kestrelhealth -> fallback-model:rw-q8-small if pool utilization > 95%. I can push the policy if Sam approves. 
Sam (oncall): go ahead. prioritize kestrelhealth. communicate to CS. 
SupportBot: Runbook snippet: https://internal.docs/runbooks/dedicated_pool_exhaustion.md -> Step 4: emergency routing / Step 6: noisy-tenant isolation. 
Mike (platform): pushing a control-plane change now. patch: 
``` 
PATCH /v1/routes/override
body: {
  "selector": "tenant:kestrelhealth",
  "fallback": "rw-q8-small",
  "condition": "pool_eu-west-1-resv-3.utilization > 0.95"
}
``` 
Anya (sre): also preparing tenant-level eviction for noisy sessions: identify top 5 tenant sessions by tokens/sec and mark preemptible. this will free ~3 GPUs worth of slots if we evict heavy background jobs. sample query: 
``` 
SELECT session_id, tokens_per_sec FROM sessions WHERE pool = 'eu-west-1-resv-3' ORDER BY tokens_per_sec DESC LIMIT 5
``` 
Jordan (cs): telling Kestrel: "we're activating emergency fallback to maintain latency, minimal quality impact, and isolating heavy background sessions. i'll provide status updates every 10m." 
Eli (runtime): autoscaler 429s look like we've hit provider soft quota for GPUs per customer. Cloud ticket has low ETA. Mitigation plan: (A) fallback routing (in flight), (B) preempt lower-priority sessions (manual eviction), (C) temporary reservation borrow from dedicated pool eu-west-1-resv-1 (needs infra approval). 
Sam (oncall): Anya — can you start eviction runbook now? mark sessions with label `noisy-background` for eviction if they have >100 tokens/sec and not in reserved list. 
Anya (sre): running eviction command now: 
``` 
POST /internal/evict_sessions
body: { "pool": "eu-west-1-resv-3", "selector": "tokens_per_sec>100 AND priority!='reserved'" }
``` 
Anya (sre): eviction started — estimate recovery ~90s to reclaim slots, notifying runtime to rebalance KV cache. 
IncidentBot: Bridge created: https://meet.link/ops-4547774321/bridge | Pager acknowledged by Sam | Priority: P1 | Impact: degraded latency for reserved tenants | ETA next update: 5m 
Mike (platform): control-plane patch applied. routing metric active. telemetry shows ~12% of Kestrel traffic now routed to rw-q8-small hosted fallback. queue length for reserved decreased from 2300 -> 1700 in 2m. good signal. 
Eli (runtime): KV cache rebalance underway. note: we may see short-term perf blips as state migrates — monitor tail latency closely. 
Jordan (cs): Kestrel responded: "thanks, we see partial return of requests, still some failures but better than before". requesting formal timeline and root cause. i've set expectation: 30-45m for full stabilization. 
Anya (sre): eviction reclaimed ~420 concurrent slots (~2 GPUs worth). reserved pool utilization now 94.7%. autoscaler 429s still present but less frequent. queue length down to 900. 
Sam (oncall): great. keep autoscale ticket open but deprioritized for immediate mitigation. next steps: 1) continue routing until cloud quota increases or cold GPUs online, 2) request infra to consider temporary borrow from resv-1, 3) postmortem owner: Anya. 
SupportBot: Logging incident: INC-2026-0432, severity P1, customer impacted: KestrelHealth (SLA track). Link to incident doc: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-0432 
Mike (platform): infra approved borrow of 1 reserved node from eu-west-1-resv-1; will be live in ~4m after placement. that should bring utilization below 90%. 
Eli (runtime): after borrow, be prepared to scale down fallbacks and re-route back to primary pool. i'll coordinate with Sam for graceful rollback. 
Sam (oncall): Ack. prepping customer-facing note and will do a short blameless summary once stabilized. thanks team. closing bridge in 15m unless new alerts. 
Jordan (cs): leaving note for account team to follow up with Kestrel for RCA and compensation if needed. 
Anya (sre): postmortem checklist assigned. collecting logs, autoscaler traces, and quota timeline. root cause candidates: provider per-account limit + noisy background sessions. will post updates to INC doc. 
IncidentBot: Update: pool utilization now 87%, queue length 120, fallback routing at 3% of traffic, borrow node active. Incident state -> mitigated. Please file postmortem within 72h.
Sam (oncall): marking as mitigated. thanks everyone — great coordination.
